name: ODDFYIELD
description: ODDFYIELD returns the yield to maturity for a bond with an irregular first coupon period.
tldr: Calculates the yield of a security with an odd first coupon period.
syntax: (settlement, maturity, issue, first_coupon, rate, pr, redemption, frequency, [basis])

parameters.name: first_coupon
parameters.description: Date of the first coupon payment.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Number of coupon payments per year (1, 2, or 4).

basicExample.description: Yield of a bond with an odd first coupon period
basicExample.explanation: Calculates the yield for a bond priced at $95 with an irregular first coupon period.

advancedExamples.title: With actual/actual basis
advancedExamples.explanation: Basis 1 is common for Treasury bonds.

howItWorks: ODDFYIELD solves for the yield that equates the present value of the bond's cash flows, including the irregular first coupon, to the purchase price.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: All dates must be valid Excel dates.
The first coupon date must be after the issue date but before maturity.

commonErrors.fix: Verify all inputs and date order.
Use DATE function or valid date serial numbers.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ODDFYIELD works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between ODDFYIELD and YIELD?
faq.answer: ODDFYIELD is for bonds with an irregular first coupon period. YIELD is for standard bonds.

faq.question: When is ODDFYIELD used?
faq.answer: It is used when a new bond issue has a first coupon period that is not standard.
